message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

**What I did and why:** I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and checked the live quote (last $420.18, bid $420.16 / ask $420.20 as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC). The filing shows a business that is large, growing, and highly cash-generative: **total revenue of $245,122 million (up 16% from $211,915 million)**, operating income of $109,433 million (+24%), net income of $88,136 million (+22%), diluted EPS of $11.80 (+22%), and operating cash flow of $118,548 million. Growth was broad-based across all three segments — Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 20% to $105,362 million on 30% Azure growth, Productivity and Business Processes rose 12% to $77,728 million, and More Personal Computing rose 13% to $62,032 million (helped by the Activision Blizzard acquisition, which added $5,729 million of revenue) — and Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $137.4 billion, up 23%. The balance sheet remains strong ($75.5 billion of cash and short-term investments, AAA-rated long-term debt), and the company returned $22.3 billion in dividends plus $12.0 billion of buybacks. Risks I noted are real but not disqualifying: heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5 billion of additions to property and equipment, with $35.4 billion of construction commitments), a $28.9 billion IRS proposed adjustment plus penalties/interest, and continued regulatory scrutiny. On balance the fundamentals support adding to the position, so I placed a single buy limit order for **20 shares of MSFT at $421.00** (just above the $420.20 ask, so it filled at $421.00 for a total of $8,420). This complies with the mandate: MSFT is an eligible ticker, it is a buy order, the notional is under the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, the limit price is within a fraction of a percent of the market price, and the purchase was funded from existing cash ($50,000 available) with no money moved out of the account.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 421.00, 20 shares = $8,420. Within $10k per order and $20k total. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.

Summary paragraph.
